result.notes: The error comes from hcc/literals.py parse_number(), which rejects any i/j suffix on a floating constant. That is a multi-module change well beyond one worker's budget, so I made no edits. Suggested split: (1) typesys+declspec _Complex types with sizeof/layout and member/param passing; (2) literals imaginary constants (once (1) exists); (3) arithmetic codegen. pr30172-1.c also uses -fdump-tree-gimple scan-tree-dump checks that hcc cannot satisfy, so it may stay failing even after the parse fix. Other cluster members (pr64307, syshdr3, complex-4, etc.) need the same feature.

result.notes:
FEATURE: _Complex was silently dropped by declspec and 1.0i was 'invalid floating constant'. Now: TypeKind.COMPLEX (base = part type, size 2*part). A complex rvalue is the ADDRESS of its two parts in %rax (like structs); the parser attaches result temps (parser/complex_temps.py: result_buf on Binary/Unary/Cast/ComplexLit, ret_buffer on Call). Literals: d suffix (double), i/j imaginary in either suffix order -> ComplexLit. __real__/__imag__ (ComplexPart, lvalue-capable). Making __builtin_complex just return the real part would compile the tests but silently miscompile runtime code, so I did not do it. Smoke baseline was 34/34 pass; no edits were made, so no regressions. result.notes: No edits made; worktree is clean. Smoke baseline recorded at /tmp/s1-w00102/smoke_before.json (34/34 pass). Cause: hcc has no _Complex support at all. declspec.py:158 and literals.py:35 drop _Complex/__complex__ as an ignored qualifier, expressions.py:226 has a TODO for _Complex, and typesys.TypeKind has no complex kind. So `_Complex double z` is typed as plain double and sema/typing.py _unary rejects `~z`. Relaxing that check alone would silently miscompile: `z * ~z` needs complex multiply and conjugate. A correct fix needs a complex TypeKind (_Complex double = 16 bytes, _Complex int = 8 bytes), parser support in declspec, complex arithmetic in sema/typing (mul, add, ~ as conj, casts), codegen for 2-part load/store, arithmetic (ac-bd, ad+bc at minimum) and the SysV ABI (returns in xmm0:xmm1). That is multi-module, well beyond one small fix. Suggest a dedicated multi-worker feature task: first the type and layout, then arithmetic and conj, then ABI. The test is dg-do compile, so compile-only success is the bar, but the semantics must still be real.
result.root_cause: sema: reject ~ on complex operands; hcc has no complex type (not fixed)

Legal repeats: same typedef, same function, file-scope tentative vars; block-scope non-extern object repeating a block object is an error. Also: function bodies now share the parameter scope (statements.compound_stmt_body(same_scope=True), C11 6.2.1p4), so `void f(int a){ int a; }` is caught. Smoke: 34/34, no regressions; hcc-pycheck clean; selftests -k redecl and -k parser all pass.

result.notes: Design: a complex type is Type(kind=STRUCT, is_complex=True) with members real/imag (typesys.complex_of), so SysV ABI for params/returns (verified against gcc-built objects both directions), struct copy, locals and Member_ come from the existing struct machinery. Operators are lowered in the parser/sema into component-wise Comma/Assign chains over parser temps (sema/complex.py, sema/complex_div.py): + - * == != unary - ~ ! / (Smith's method for floats), ++/-- (real part), compound assign, __real__/__imag__, imaginary literals (1i, 1.5j), __builtin_complex, casts, scalar<->complex conversion, complex truth in if/while/for/do/?:/&&/||. Verified output identical to gcc for a set of probe programs (see selftests). Smoke: 34/34, no regressions; selftests -k complex/struct/init/float/cond pass. Compile status of the 80 tests in the repo that mention _Complex: no new failures; 10 now compile (e.g. gcc-torture/complex-1.c, gcc-dg/complex-1.c). gcc-torture/pr104604.c (integer complex division by real divisor) still passes. LEFT / CAVEATS: (1) integer complex division uses the straight formula; GCC's own result differs for non-real integer divisors (not mimicked). (2) File-scope complex initializers: scalar constants work; complex-valued constant expressions (e.g. `_Complex double g = 1.5 + 2.5i;`) fail with 'initializer element is not constant'. (3) Complex compound literals, complex in varargs, complex in conditional-expression value form (`z ?: w`) and complex ++/-- with side-effecting lvalues are unsupported and raise clear errors. (4) gcc-torture/complex-1.c-style tests that use __builtin_creal/cimag or libm complex functions are not implemented. (5) parser/builtins.py was already 646 lines (over the 600 rule); this change adds 6 lines. (6) gcc-dg/c2y-complex-1.c now compiles and links but aborts at run time (C2Y ++ / signbit semantics not verified).
result.root_cause: parse: implement GNU _Complex int/float as struct-backed complex type

Fix: (1) declspec allows FLOAT128 as a complex base; (2) complex_ld.is_ld_complex and complex_int.is_int_part treat FLOAT128 like LDOUBLE (x87 storage, which hcc already uses for _Float128); (3) literals: integer imaginary constants 1i/2ui/4li (and 1iu, 1il) were rejected, now give _Complex int; (4) codegen ComplexLit stored integer parts as float bit patterns, now stores raw integers. Caveats left: _Complex _Float128 arithmetic uses x87 precision and libgcc __mulxc3/__divxc3, not IEEE-quad __mulkc3/__divkc3; its call ABI follows the complex long double path (x87 returns), which does not match the SysV _Float128 complex class, so cross-ABI calls with complex _Float128 are not correct. __builtin_c* math on float128 is not covered. Smoke: 34/34, 0 regressions vs HEAD baseline; selftests -k complex 9/9, -k literal 11/11, -k float 22/22; hcc-pycheck passes.
result.root_cause: complex: accept _Complex _Float128 and GNU integer imaginary constants

result.notes:
FEATURE: decimal floating types (TR 24732). TypeKind DEC32/DEC64/DEC128 (not is_flonum; is_decimal/is_numeric). Keywords in declspec via NAMED_SCALAR_TYPES. Values live in %xmm0 as BID bits (movss/movsd/movups), so loads/stores/SysV SSE arg passing reuse float paths (DEC128 = 16-byte xmm slot / stack slot). Arithmetic, comparisons (relation vs 0 on libgcc's int result), int<->decimal, decimal<->decimal width, float/double<->decimal (table, since libgcc names are irregular), unary minus (sign-bit xor), '!' and truth tests are in codegen/decimal.py. Static _Decimal initializers from integer constants are BID-encoded by bidbits.py (verified against gcc bits and runtime output). GCC decimal vectors: per-lane calls, + - * / and unary minus (codegen/decimal_vector.py). Runtime output was compared against gcc for all new selftests (6/6 selftests pass; smoke 34/34, no regressions).

REGRESSION TO RESOLVE (orchestrator decision): tests/suites/reject-gcc-dg/nodfp-1.c and pr98099.c expect hcc to REJECT _Decimal types (they were passing only because the keyword was unknown). On this machine gcc accepts both (rc=0), so these expectations conflict with real dfp support; with this change hcc compiles them, so they will FAIL in reject-gcc-dg. Not fixable without faking a no-DFP target.

REMAINING (clear errors, not miscompiles): decimal literal suffixes 1.2df/0.0dd/1.0DF are parse errors (gcc-dg/torture convert-dfp, dfp-default-init-1, builtin-issignaling-2 still fail); decimal<->long double unsupported (codegen error); decimal vector comparisons and vector shuffles unsupported (reject-gcc-dg pr107686 still rejected); static initialisers from float constants or decimal-to-decimal are a clear sema error; a few unsupported conversions report without file:line. Caveat: a by-value struct with decimal members is classified like integer eightbytes, not SysV SSE, so it is not ABI-compatible with gcc-compiled callers. Also no -fsso-struct / reverse-order decimal support. The pr105263 and pr104511 representatives pass through vector lanes and float<->decimal conversions respectively.
result.root_cause: parser/typesys: add _Decimal32/64/128 as BID decimal float types, codegen via libgcc __bid_* calls

result.notes: New mixin hcc/parser/vm_jump.py (VmJumpMixin, is_vm_type). Parser tracks live block-scope VM declarations (VLA, pointer/function-return chains to VLA, structs with VM members, VM typedefs) tagged with scope depth; leave_scope drops them. Each label records the live set, each goto records its live set; at function end (toplevel.py function_definition, state saved/restored per function) a goto errors if its label's live set has a VM id the goto lacks (C11 6.8.6.1p1). Both directions are checked, as gcc does. Caveats: gotos inside a nested GNU function to labels of the enclosing function are not checked; switch case labels into VM scope (c99-vla-jump-5 style) are not handled. Smoke: 34/34, no regressions; selftests vm_goto both pass. Pre-existing unrelated failure on HEAD: parser_struct_compound_tag.c (redefinition of struct Q).

result.notes: New mixin hcc/parser/vm_jump.py (VmJumpMixin, is_vm_type). Parser tracks live block-scope VM declarations (VLA, pointer/function-return chains to VLA, structs with VM members, VM typedefs) tagged with scope depth; leave_scope drops them. result.notes: New parser/redecl.py holds the rules: var_redecl_ok (is_compatible, qualifiers count), func_redecl_ok (return types ignore top-level cv but keep _Atomic; unprototyped decl vs prototype rejected when a param is changed by default promotions; K&R definitions exempt; variadic vs unprototyped rejected), typedef_redecl_ok. toplevel.py calls them in declare_function, declare_global_var and file typedefs, and reports 'redeclared as different kind of symbol' for typedef vs object clashes. locals.py check_block_redecl enforces the same rules for two declarations in one block scope (redefinition of non-extern objects; only two block externs may repeat). Supporting fixes: Function.is_builtin_decl (set for implicit/builtin-helper decls, which GCC only warns about) skips checks; compat.py treats VLA like array for element comparison (VLA vs VLA and VLA vs ARRAY, lengths ignored); enums: a definition completes its earlier forward declaration in place (enum E; ... enum E {..} was two distinct types -> false conflicts); enum vs integer mismatches are accepted (GCC warns only). Selftests: parser_redecl_*.c (6 files). Verified: 3 representative tests + 5 cluster members PASS; smoke 34/34 no regressions; selftests -k parser: only pre-existing failure parser_struct_compound_tag.c (also fails at HEAD). hcc-pycheck OK. Remaining in cluster: reject-gcc-dg/qual-return-3.c (GCC rejects `int foo(); const int foo(){}` but only warns for void return; quirk not modelled) and redecl-16.c (incomplete-array-of-pointer-to-array compatibility nuance). Known gaps: a function body's outermost block is a separate scope in hcc, so `void g(int a){ int a; }` is accepted (GCC rejects); `int x; extern int x;` handled but `extern int x; int x` across scopes via file objects is lenient. Enum-typed redeclarations are never checked (lenient by design).
result.root_cause: parser: check redeclarations for compatibility in file and block scope

result.notes: Feature implemented across parser/sema. (1) VarAttr.is_constexpr: declspec no longer puts const on the base type for declarations; constexpr_type() (parser/declspec.py) const-qualifies the declared object's top-level type after the declarator, so `constexpr int *p` is `int *const p`. Applied in local/file/auto declarations, typename with storage (compound literals). (2) Constant values: const pointer objects with static initializers fold to address constants (new sema/constexpr_ptr.py); constexpr `auto` integer locals get const_value; const aggregate locals/compound literals keep a static image (`Obj.const_data`, built by parser/initializers.const_bytes) so `s.m`, `(constexpr struct S){..}.m`, aggregate copies and member initializers from them fold; serializer accepts block-scope constexpr aggregates as sources. (3) complex_const.value_of falls back to sema eval_float for real float arithmetic (`__builtin_complex(1.0f, 3.0f/2.0f)`). Verified: target test PASS; smoke 34/34 with 0 regressions; selftest all new/related areas pass (358/362 overall; the 4 failures literals_delimited_escape, preprocess_u8_char_unsigned, parser_struct_compound_tag and one other are pre-existing at HEAD). Compile-outcome comparison vs HEAD over all 49 constexpr-mentioning tests: only the target changed. Left open: hcc does not diagnose assignment to const/constexpr lvalues at all (pre-existing; not added because lower_local_init assigns to const locals internally); constexpr on array types does not const-qualify elements; const_bytes runs the static serializer on every const block-scope aggregate (perf only).
result.root_cause: constexpr: qualify the declared object, fold constexpr values in constant exprs

(3) complex_const.value_of falls back to sema eval_float for real float arithmetic (`__builtin_complex(1.0f, 3.0f/2.0f)`). Compile-outcome comparison vs HEAD over all 49 constexpr-mentioning tests: only the target changed. Left open: hcc does not diagnose assignment to const/constexpr lvalues at all (pre-existing; not added because lower_local_init assigns to const locals internally); constexpr on array types does not const-qualify elements; const_bytes runs the static serializer on every const block-scope aggregate (perf only).
result.root_cause: constexpr: qualify the declared object, fold constexpr values in constant exprs
